narrativeReportMd:
# decimal R4→R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
`decimal` has one local hard instance-breaking change: the primitive value regex was narrowed in R6 to impose finite limits on integer digits, fractional digits, and exponent digits. Existing R4 instances that used very long decimal lexical forms can become invalid under R6 StructureDefinition-based validation.

## Scope
I compared the supplied R4 and R6 `StructureDefinition/decimal` files, package metadata, package indexes, and supporting generated R6 OpenAPI/XML schema artifacts. The canonical identity remains stable. The R6 base-definition change to `PrimitiveType` is a global primitive/base hierarchy change and is excluded from `findings[]` under the inherited-base scope rule.

## Main migration themes
The practical migration issue is lexical precision/length. R4 allowed unbounded digits in the integer part, fraction, and exponent. R6 limits the integer part to either `0` or 1-18 non-leading-zero digits, the fractional part to 1-17 digits, and the exponent to 1-9 digits. Systems should test high-precision measurements, calculated values, scoring values, and financial factors before validating R4 data as R6.

## Highest-impact findings
The sole high-impact local finding is `decimal:VALUE_CONSTRAINT:decimal.value:a6d2f1`, the narrowed regex on `decimal.value`.

## Findings requiring human review
No local finding requires human review to confirm that the computable regex changed. Human review would improve understanding of the ballot rationale and whether implementations should round, reject, or preserve out-of-range historical values outside core R6 instances.

## Backward-compatible design observations
The R6 limit may be intended to make decimal implementation limits explicit and portable. A less disruptive approach could have kept the R4 lexical regex in the base datatype and expressed finite implementation limits as guidance, warnings, or profile constraints, but that would not give all R6 validators the same enforceable boundary.

## Follow-up analysis
Assess the new `PrimitiveType`/`DataType` hierarchy separately, and check high-value decimal usages in resource/datatype reports where local element semantics make precision loss safety-critical.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: `decimal` keeps its canonical identity but R6 narrows the allowed lexical form. The main migration concern is R4 data with more than 18 integer digits, more than 17 fractional digits, or more than 9 exponent digits. The main uncertainty is the ballot rationale and how generated schemas/validators will enforce the StructureDefinition regex.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration should focus on detecting decimal values that are valid under the R4 regex but invalid under the R6 regex. Remediation is domain-specific: some systems can round or rescale values, some must preserve high-precision source values outside core R6 decimal fields, and some should reject or quarantine records rather than silently truncating clinically or financially meaningful precision.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for the local computable delta because both StructureDefinitions directly declare the old and new regex on `decimal.value`, and the R6 generated OpenAPI schema mirrors the narrower pattern. Confidence is lower for rationale and exact runtime prevalence because no official diff, narrative ballot note, terminology expansion, or validator test suite was supplied.

findings.title: decimal.value regex now limits integer, fractional, and exponent digit counts

oldState.summary: R4 allowed an unbounded number of digits in the integer part, fractional part, and exponent.
oldState.narrativeMd: In R4, `decimal.value` used a lexical regex that prohibited leading zero forms but did not impose a finite digit count. Values such as `1234567890123456789`, `1.123456789012345678`, `0.000000000000000001`, or `1e1000000000` matched the primitive regex.

newState.summary: R6 limits the integer part to 18 digits, the fractional part to 17 digits, and the exponent to 9 digits.
newState.narrativeMd: In R6, `decimal.value` keeps the same primitive path, cardinality, and FHIRPath type, but the regex now rejects lexical forms exceeding the explicit digit limits.

facts.oldValue: unbounded when a decimal point is present
facts.newValue: 1-17 when a decimal point is present

facts.oldValue: unbounded when an exponent is present

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The old and new elements have the same `id`, `path`, primitive FHIRPath type, representation, and cardinality; only the regex extension on the primitive value type changes materially.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a direct validation narrowing. Any R4 instance containing a decimal lexical token with 19 or more integer digits, 18 or more fractional digits, or 10 or more exponent digits can pass the R4 primitive regex but fail the R6 primitive regex. The datatype is widely reused across resources and complex datatypes, so strict validators, generated parsers, code generators, database constraints, and migration pipelines that rely on the R6 StructureDefinition may reject historical R4 data. R6-valid decimal lexical forms remain representable by the broader R4 regex, so the round-trip risk is primarily R4-to-R6, not R6-to-R4.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The risk depends on where the decimal is used. High-precision scientific measurements, calculations, scores, or financial factors could be affected; many routine clinical decimal values will fall within the new limits.

justification.inferredGoal: Make decimal implementation limits explicit and more portable across validators, generated schemas, databases, and languages.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep the R4 broad regex but add a base warning, best-practice invariant, or minimum-support statement for the finite portable digit limits.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The likely R6 goal is reasonable: an unbounded primitive decimal lexical space is difficult to support consistently across validators, generated schemas, databases, and language runtimes. Because R4 allowed arbitrarily long integer, fractional, and exponent parts, any enforceable finite base bound necessarily rejects some R4-valid instances. The exact R6 thresholds are not fully explained by the supplied evidence, so this is not fully `Justified`, but the level of breakage is probably reasonable if the goal was a single portable base primitive contract rather than advisory implementation guidance.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base design would keep the R4 regex and express the 18-integer-digit, 17-fractional-digit, and 9-exponent-digit limits as a warning-level invariant, best-practice rule, or declared minimum portable support boundary. That would preserve existing R4-valid values and still signal the interoperability risk, but it would not make over-limit values invalid in base R6. Profile-only constraints, migration transforms, or preserving over-limit source values in extensions are useful mitigations, not full backward-compatible base-design alternatives. The partial alternative therefore trades compatibility for persistent validation ambiguity and inconsistent downstream implementation limits.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves R4 instances, but leaves nonportable high-precision decimals valid and weakens uniform validator, schema, database, and codegen behavior.

evidence.detail: R4 decimal.value regex has unbounded digit repetitions for integer, fraction, and exponent components.
R6 decimal.value regex caps integer, fraction, and exponent digit counts.
The generated R6 OpenAPI schema repeats the narrowed decimal pattern, indicating downstream schema/codegen surfaces may also see the new limit.

evidence.locator: StructureDefinition snapshot elements with type.code == decimal
evidence.detail: A local scan found many decimal-typed elements in both packages, confirming that a primitive-level decimal regex change can surface broadly across resource and datatype validation.

examples.examplesMd: The examples are lexical decimal tokens represented as strings only so the report preserves exact digit counts. In real FHIR JSON they would appear as unquoted JSON numbers in decimal-valued elements, while in XML they would appear in a `value` attribute.

findings.narrativeMd: `decimal.value` changed from an effectively unbounded lexical decimal regex to a bounded one. This is not merely documentation: validators that apply the StructureDefinition regex can reject high-precision R4 data that was valid before. The most surprising cases are small fractional values with many leading fractional zeros, very large integer values, or very large exponents; none of those require unusual element structure, only a decimal token whose lexical length exceeds the new R6 limits.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4-valid instance can become R6-invalid if any decimal-valued element contains a lexical form outside the new bounds. R6-valid values are still accepted by the broader R4 regex, so R6-to-R4 representability for the primitive value itself is not materially reduced. Runtime behavior may differ by tooling: StructureDefinition-aware FHIR validators should enforce the regex, while generic JSON Schema tooling may not enforce the OpenAPI `pattern` when the schema type is `number`; XML schema support seen in the R6 package uses `xs:decimal xs:double` and does not show the same regex restriction.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Before validating R4 data as R6, scan all decimal-valued elements for integer parts longer than 18 digits, fractional parts longer than 17 digits, and exponent parts longer than 9 digits. Do not silently round or truncate without domain review. If precision is clinically, scientifically, or financially significant, preserve the original value in an extension, source document, audit trail, or profile-specific representation and decide whether the R6 core decimal field should be omitted, rounded with provenance, or rejected.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change could have been made less disruptive by leaving the R4 regex in place and adding advisory implementation limits or profile-level constraints. That alternative would preserve existing high-precision data but would not establish a single enforceable base primitive contract. Given only the supplied definitions, the exact choice of 18 integer digits, 17 fractional digits, and 9 exponent digits cannot be fully justified or rejected.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The R6 package is a ballot build. If the final R6 package changes the decimal regex, this finding should be refreshed. Also verify official validator behavior for JSON decimal lexical preservation, because JSON parsers may lose the original numeric token text before validation.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `decimal.value` keeps the same primitive path, cardinality, and FHIRPath type, but R6 narrows the lexical regex from unbounded integer, fractional, and exponent digit runs to explicit caps. A strict validator or generated schema using the R6 package can therefore reject R4 decimal tokens such as a 19-digit integer, an 18-digit fractional tail, or a 10-digit exponent. The affected lexical forms are likely uncommon in routine clinical exchange, and the published datatype notes say regexes are informative rather than normative, so this is not necessarily a universal runtime failure. Still, `decimal` is a normative primitive used across many datatypes and resources, and the R6 package and OpenAPI schema make the narrower pattern visible to validators and code generators. Without supplied rationale showing why over-limit R4 values must become base-invalid rather than warning-level/non-portable, this normative primitive narrowing deserves standards/design review.
keyEvidence: R4 maturity map records `decimal` as standardsStatus `normative` with normativeVersion `4.0.0`; the task supplied R4 FMM/status as normative.
R6 OpenAPI `definitions.decimal.pattern` repeats the narrowed pattern, so downstream schema/tooling surfaces can enforce it.

HL7 R4 and current build datatype pages checked: both note decimal precision matters, large/highly precise values are rare in medicine, and regexes are informative rather than normative; the current build page also presents the bounded decimal regex.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Normative R4 status raises the burden of justification for a base primitive narrowing. The uncommon nature of over-limit values and the informative-regex note soften the practical prevalence estimate, but they do not remove the stability concern because package-driven validators and generated schemas can still reject formerly accepted R4 data.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 decimal lexical forms matching the old unbounded regex but exceeding R6 digit caps can fail R6 StructureDefinition/OpenAPI-pattern validation; some implementations may experience this mainly as schema/tooling break because published datatype notes treat regexes as informative.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A plausible less-breaking base design would retain the R4 regex and express the finite portable limits as guidance, a best-practice/warning-level rule, or a declared interoperability support boundary. That would preserve R4 instances while still flagging values likely to be non-portable. The tradeoff is real: it would not give R6 a single hard base contract for validators, databases, and code generators. Given the normative primitive status and unclear supplied rationale for making the caps hard-invalid, the alternative is strong enough to warrant revisit.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: I agree with the existing report that the regex delta is real, R4-to-R6 directed, and potentially high impact for strict validation/tooling. I qualify the impact because official datatype notes describe regexes as informative and the affected values appear uncommon, and I place more weight on the less-breaking warning/advisory-base alternative than the existing probably-justified framing.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: Canonical URL, id, name, kind, type, derivation, abstract flag, and active status remain stable. The baseDefinition changed from `Element` to `PrimitiveType`, but that is intentionally excluded as a base hierarchy issue.
The local snapshot element set remains `decimal`, `decimal.id`, `decimal.extension`, and `decimal.value`; no local element was added, removed, renamed, moved, split, or merged.
All decimal elements retain the same cardinalities: root `0..*`, `id` `0..1`, `extension` `0..*`, and `value` `0..1`.

`decimal.id` remains FHIRPath `System.String`, `decimal.extension` remains `Extension`, and `decimal.value` remains FHIRPath `System.Decimal`. The material type extension change is the value regex, reported under value limits.
`decimal` has no Reference-typed elements or target profiles.
No local ElementDefinition invariant was added or removed on `decimal.value`. Inherited `ele-1`/`ext-1` wording and xpath metadata differences are scoped out to base artifact reports.
No fixed value, pattern value, or default value appears on the decimal elements in either version.
The relevant elements remain `isModifier: false`; no modifier reason was introduced.
The relevant elements remain `isSummary: false`; there is no summary flag change.
No slicing is declared on `decimal` in either version.

The core definition and decimal-specific implementation comment are materially unchanged. Metadata description/publisher/jurisdiction text changed, and inherited extension-definition wording changed, but no additional local semantic break was found beyond the regex.

Element representation remains `xmlAttr` for `id` and `value`. The lexical regex narrowing has serialization/runtime consequences and is reported as the main finding; no separate element representation change was found.

The R6 decimal regex is a subset of the R4 regex for primitive lexical values, so an R6-valid decimal value is representable as an R4 decimal value. The material break is old broad R4 values failing new narrower R6 validation.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 adds decimal type-characteristic metadata
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: R6 adds `structuredefinition-type-characteristics` extensions with `has-range`, `is-continuous`, and `has-length`. These are metadata on the StructureDefinition rather than required instance content, so they do not by themselves make old instances invalid.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Code generators, documentation generators, or validation planners may use these characteristics to model decimal as ordered, continuous, and length-constrained. This aligns with the regex-limit finding but is not a separate instance-level break.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 updates descriptive/package metadata
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The R6 artifact updates package/version metadata, publisher/contact information, jurisdiction, generated narrative text, and short description wording. These do not change the local element model or primitive value semantics apart from the reported regex.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Metadata-sensitive tooling should expect R6 ballot package labels such as `6.0.0-ballot4` and `notForPublication`, but instance migration is not affected by these fields.
